claims.statement: The European Solar Charter identifies concentrated import dependence and supply-chain resilience as issues and calls for cooperation across manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, installers, and offtakers.

contrary_evidence: The charter is voluntary and does not grant a purchasing club any allocation right.
The cited source also describes price pressure on European producers, so resilient or diversified supply may cost more than spot imports.

economics.acquisition_route: Founder-family installer proof point, distributor referrals, installer training groups, and regional peer invitations
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is hundreds of installer members, several billion PLN of influenced procurement over time, and recurring membership and transaction revenue with retained ownership
economics.founder_time: Initially 10-18 hours per week with forecasting automated and contract negotiation supported by counsel
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 55-75% on membership and service fees if inventory ownership and take-or-pay exposure remain limited
economics.payback: Unvalidated; 20-40 paying members may cover setup depending on supplier deposit terms
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 10000-30000 PLN annual membership plus 1-3% reservation or procurement fee and disclosed supplier rebates
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual membership and repeated project allocations; value falls when ordinary spot supply is consistently sufficient

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Committed member demand, fulfillment history, supplier contracts, and allocation data increase negotiating leverage and switching cost
fingerprint.customer: Independent Polish solar and storage installers too small to negotiate reliable supply terms alone
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Recruit installers through the family business, wholesalers, training partners, and regional trade referrals
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Pooled forecasts, negotiated allocation windows, member reservation portal, supplier diversification, and release of unused slots before liability crystallizes
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Members pay an annual fee and reservation premium when exercising an allocation; suppliers may also pay transparent volume rebates
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An installer wins a project and needs compliant equipment on a fixed date but lacks purchasing leverage or diversified allocation

founder_fit: Direct access to installer purchasing behavior through the family company
Forecasting and allocation optimization use data-science skills
Can start without a warehouse or speculative stock
Member-led distribution reduces dependence on personal branding
risks: Take-or-pay or deposit obligations could exceed available capital
Purchasing coordination must avoid unlawful price or market coordination
Supplier failure or product defects can damage all members
Low spot prices may make membership unattractive

structure.control_point: Contractual priority inventory allocations and pooled offtake options
structure.critical_dependency: Suppliers must honor useful reservation terms while member forecasts are accurate enough to avoid take-or-pay losses

thesis: Pool forecast demand from independent Polish solar installers and negotiate priority allocation or release-window contracts with selected manufacturers and distributors, selling members supply assurance without initially carrying speculative inventory.
title: Installer Priority-Allocation Purchasing Club
uncertainties: No supplier has offered transferable or priority allocations
Unknown installer willingness to commit forecasts and fees
Unknown frequency and economic cost of supply disruption in target categories
Competition-law and rebate-disclosure structure requires review
